newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TO ALLOW INDIA NO RESPITE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TO ALLOW INDIA NO RESPITE.

text.p: The bad news for Sachin Tendulkar's embattled Indian team is that their South African opponents have made a New Year's resolution to play even better.

Leading the series 2-0 going into the third and final test at the Wanderers, South Africa's coach Bob Woolmer said: "Our New Year's resolution is to become a more consistent team. We may be two-nil up, but that was last year and we really want to win this one."

On the same ground in December 1992, in South Africa's second home test since readmission, the two sides fought out a draw in which Tendulkar made a brilliant century and a young Hansie Cronje fared less impressively.

Four years down the line Cronje is struggling again, but Woolmer is not concerned. "Hansie is a very important member of the side. His runs are important, but as a leader and a motivator he probably starts every test 60 not out anyway."
It is a different story for Tendulkar who, along with Mohammad Azharuddin, bears the responsibility of having to make a big score every time he goes to the crease.

Indian coach Madan Lal is shrugging off the disappointment of going into the test playing only for pride. "What has happened is history. We are practicing well and looking positively at the match," he said.
But while South Africa can enjoy the luxury of going into the game with, in all probability, an unchanged side, India have the problem of a lack of alternatives.
At the top of the order Vikram Rathore is set to replace Workeri Raman on the back of a century and a 50 against Free State in the last warm up game.

But there are no other ways to stiffen a batting order that has shied away from the pace of the South Africans and the selectors will be once again rueing the decision to bring three wicket-keepers on tour.
The bowling attack will almost certainly be the same which did duty in Cape Town, with Doda Ganesh again being preferred as third seamer to David Johnson.
The omens are not good for the Indians and the chances are that, without some serious intervention from the weather, South Africa will be celebrating their first ever three-nil series win.
South Africa: Gary Kirsten, Andrew Hudson, Adam Bacher, Daryll Cullinan, Hansie Cronje (captain), Brian McMillan, Shaun Pollock, Dave Richardson, Lance Klusener, Allan Donald, Paul Adams.
India: Nayan Mongia, Vikram Rathore, Saurav Ganguly, Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Rahul Dravid, Mohammad Azharuddin, V.V.S. Laxman, Anil Kumble, Javagal Srinath, Venkatesh Prasad, Doda Ganesh.
